nodes.summary: If $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a Hanner polytope, then $0 < n$.
nodes.title: Hanner polytopes live in positive dimension

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Hanner cross-polytope $P_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is a Hanner polytope.
nodes.title: The Hanner cross-polytopes are Hanner polytopes

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Hanner cross-polytope $P_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is defined by recursion on $n$: $P_0$ is the centered unit segment $[-1, 1] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^1$, and $P_{n+1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+2}$ is the $\ell_1$ sum of $P_n$ and the centered unit segment.
nodes.title: Hanner cross-polytope

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Hanner cube $C_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ equals the coordinate cube $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1} : -1 \le x_i \le 1 \text{ for every } i\} = [-1, 1]^{n+1}$.
nodes.title: The Hanner cube is the coordinate cube

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Hanner cube $C_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is a Hanner polytope.
nodes.title: The Hanner cubes are Hanner polytopes

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Hanner cube $C_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is defined by recursion on $n$: $C_0$ is the centered unit segment $[-1, 1] \subseteq \mathbb{R}^1$, and $C_{n+1} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{n+2}$ is the $\ell_\infty$ sum of $C_n$ and the centered unit segment.
nodes.title: Hanner cube

nodes.summary: For sets $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ and $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the $\ell_\infty$ sum of $K$ and $L$ is the set of points of $\mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ whose first $m$ coordinates form a point of $K$ and whose last $n$ coordinates form a point of $L$; that is, the product $K \times L$ under the identification $\mathbb{R}^{m+n} = \mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$.
nodes.title: $\ell_\infty$ sum of bodies

nodes.summary: For sets $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ and $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the $\ell_1$ sum of $K$ and $L$ is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ of $(K \times \{0\}) \cup (\{0\} \times L)$, where $\mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ is identified with $\mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ by splitting off the first $m$ coordinates.
nodes.title: $\ell_1$ sum of bodies

nodes.summary: The centered unit segment is the closed unit ball $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^1 : \|x\| \le 1\}$, that is, the segment $[-1, 1]$. It is the one-dimensional leaf in the recursive definition of Hanner polytopes.
nodes.title: Centered unit segment

nodes.summary: For $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ and $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, identify $\mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ with $\mathbb{R}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ by splitting off the first $m$ coordinates; the $\ell_\infty$ sum of $K$ and $L$ is $K \times L$, and their $\ell_1$ sum is the convex hull of $(K \times \{0\}) \cup (\{0\} \times L)$, both viewed as subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{m+n}$. The Hanner polytopes are the smallest family of subsets…
nodes.title: Hanner polytopes

nodes.summary: Let $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$ and $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$. A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ lies in the $\ell_\infty$ Hanner sum of $K$ and $L$ if and only if $(x_1, \dots, x_m) \in K$ and $(x_{m+1}, \dots, x_{m+n}) \in L$.
nodes.title: Membership in the $\ell_\infty$ Hanner sum

nodes.summary: A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^1$ lies in the Hanner unit segment if and only if every coordinate $x_i$ of $x$ satisfies $|x_i| \le 1$.
nodes.title: Membership in the Hanner unit segment

nodes.summary: Every Hanner polytope $K$ is centrally symmetric about the origin: $-K = K$.
nodes.title: Hanner polytopes are centrally symmetric

nodes.summary: For every Hanner polytope $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $-x \in K$ if and only if $x \in K$.
nodes.title: Negation preserves membership in a Hanner polytope

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every Hanner polytope $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, the origin is an interior point of $K$.
nodes.title: Hanner polytopes contain the origin in their interior

nodes.summary: The origin belongs to every Hanner polytope.
nodes.title: Hanner polytopes contain the origin

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
